This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of M.V.Act praying to call for the records in MVC.No.329/2013, from the file of Court of Senior Civil Judge &
Addl.MACT, Turuvekere and thereby allow the claim petition of the appellants by awarding compensation as prayed in the claim petition by modifying the judgment and award dated 20.01.2020 to meet the ends of justice and equity.

2

This Miscellaneous First Appeal coming on for Admission through Physical Hearing/Video Conferencing, this day, the Court delivered the following:
 ORDER
The learned counsel for the appellants is neither present physically nor through Video Conference.

2. Learned counsel for respondent No.3 alone is physically present in the Court and submits that in view of no liability fixed upon the present respondent No.3 by the Tribunal and the sole liability was fixed upon respondent Nos.1 and 2, against whom, the present appeal has stood dismissed, the appeal is not maintainable.

3. A perusal of the impugned judgment would go to show that the present appellants as claimants have instituted a claim petition before the learned Senior Civil Judge and Addl.Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Turuvekere, under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation towards the alleged death of one Sri Harish @ Harish Kumar, in a road traffic accident said to have been occurred on 22.07.2012.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and Addl.Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Turuvekere
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondent Nos.1, 2 and 3 before the Tribunal are also the respondent Nos.1, 2 and 3 in this appeal, who were shown respectively as the insured, R.C. owner and the insurer of the motorcycle respectively.

After contest, the Tribunal by its impugned judgment and award dated 20.01.2020, though has proceeded to award compensation of a sum of `16,45,000/- to the claimants, however, it fastened the liability only as against respondent Nos.1 and 2 by observing that the insurer of the offending motorcycle i.e., respondent No.3 is not liable to pay compensation amount to the claimants before it.

4. This Court on 10.03.2023 by observing that the appellants have failed to take appropriate steps against respondents Nos.1 and 2 for issuance of emergent notice against them, had by a reasoned order, dismissed the appeal as against respondent Nos.1 and 2 for not taking steps and it also observed that the maintainability of the appeal only as against respondent No.3 (Insurance Company) was required to be heard.

In spite of the same, the appellant till date has not filed any application seeking recalling of the said order dated 10.03.2023 and seeking permission to take appropriate steps to ensure the service of emergent notice upon respondent Nos.1 and 2.

On the other hand, it appears that, five days thereafter i.e., after passing of the order of dismissal against respondent No.1 and 2, on 15.03.2023, the appellant has paid the process in the registry for issuance of notice to respondent Nos.1 and 2.
Needless to say that, when the order of dismissal of the appeal as against respondent Nos.1 and 2 is passed, the question of issuing notice to respondent Nos.1 and 2 does not arise.
As such, merely because the appellant has paid the process after the dismissal of appeal against respondent Nos.1 and 2, the same would not on its own resulting recalling the order dated 10.03.2023.
Thus, the appeal as against respondent No.3-Insurance Company alone, against whom no liability was fastened by the Tribunal, is not maintainable.

Further the learned counsel for the appellant also has remained absent without showing any reasons.
As such, the Appeal stands dismissed as not maintainable as against the sole remaining respondent No.3.
